body:
I have some of cloud variables in my unshared project. Here's the link: [url=https://scratch.mit.edu/projects/319084584/]https://scratch.mit.edu/projects/319084584/[/url].\
Here's what I am trying to do:\
I store the world record holder username in one cloud variable, and store the number of letters in the second. I have to use either a function or a loop to determine the world record holder username. However, when I decode, trailing zeroes may have already been removed, so I have to add the number of trailing zeroes that corresponds with the current number (by subtraction), then use it with the character list to decode the world record variable. Here's how I encode it:\
\
First, it should look at one character of the username, which will then look for where it is in the characters variable (I plan on making it easier by changing it to a list later on)*, then use that number (the position in the string), subtract 1, and convert to binary, making sure trailing zeroes add in for a total of 6 digits (I saw a few projects on it). I do this for each character of the username, adding it to a list which I haven't created just yet, and once I finished it for each character, I combine the 6-digit binary strings corresponding to the letter (A is 000000, B is 000001, z is 111101, - is 111110, _ is 111111) (using a function that supplies a loop I haven't created just yet), then convert the combined string number back to decimal. I just realized just now that converting it to hexadecimal and then to decimal is essentially the same and also pointless having to add an extra step in between.\
\
*When I first created this project, I didn't know that there was [url=https://en.scratch-wiki.info/wiki/Item_Number_of_()_in_()_(block)]this block[/url] to ever exist. I mean to not use a loop to check IF that letter of the username is the same as THAT letter of the character string.\
\
To decode, I want to decode it back to binary, then convert it to a new list, then use the [scratchblocks]insert [] at (1 v) of [list v][/scratchblocks] block to insert trailing zeroes back into the list (NOT replace), which I can use a repeat loop at the same time to insert the right number of trailing zeroes in all at once. However, I have to determine that number for the loop by multiplying the number of characters in the world record holder username by 6 (because 6 bits for each character), then use that new number and make it so that new number MINUS the number of digits in the binary conversion in the cloud record variable (due to removed trailing zeroes), to get a new number. That new number, I use to add the right amount of trailing zeroes by using the repeat until () block along with the number that was created, then split it back into chunks of 6 and put each chunk in yet another new list, then convert the number back to decimal, then put these decimal numbers in a new list, replace them with themselves added up by 1, then create a new list composed of each decimal number (the new ones that are the old ones that were just added up by 1), then find what character it is in the characters variable (or list), then copy that character into a new list (or if it the second letter and up, the same new list just created, not the decimal number one). After that, combine it back up into a string that contains the username, and store it in the world record holder until the page is refreshed or whatever.\
\
I do not need help combining anything (that is easy), but after I insert the trailing zeroes automatically into the list, I need help splitting it back up into chunks of 6. I may make a new variable for the chunks themselves, then put it into a chunk list. I will then replace the chunk with a new chunk created for each character one at a time and add it to the list. However, I have to use a loop and yet another variable (for determining how many chunks already done and then multiplying it by 6) to make it not pass 6 characters in one variable. Before and after that, I also need help converting decimal to binary and binary to decimal.

name: Trying to make a project to store \world record holder\" in a variable"
body:
Anyway, I think I have a plan for how I can do it with decimal.\
Set up conversions and chunks (I don't want to use case sensing anymore):\
Create a list called [scratchblocks](conversions::list)[/scratchblocks], making sure to add the right content inside. Then, I will use an encoding and decoding script.\
Encoding script (uses a block that exists in Scratch 3.0 and needs to have \::list\" at the end to make it compatible with Scratch 2.0)

name: [scratchblocks]
define encode (string)
set [i v] to [1]
set [world record holder variable v] to []
repeat (length of (string))
if <(item # of (letter (i) of (string)) in [conversions v]::list) < (10)> then

name: Cloud Drag and Drop!
body:
Link: https://scratch.mit.edu/projects/321109488/\
\
Drag the Scratch Cat. You can watch someone else drag at the same time.\
\
In order to use cloud data, you must be a Scratcher and be logged in to that account. If your profile says New Scratcher, you must have a verified email address, have a few shared projects, be on Scratch for at least 2 weeks, but usually one month, be active on the website to some degree, and have comments and forum posts. (The last one isn't necessary, but it does help.)\
\
To prevent two devices/people from dragging at the same time, a cloud variable is set to 1 when a drag starts, and set to 0 when it ends. When you try to drag, it checks if the cloud variable is 1, if so, it sends a message.\
\

\

name: Automatic project copy detector
body:
[quote=DarthVader4Life][quote=46009361][quote=DarthVader4Life] -snip- [/quote]\
Would be easy to code, but this would be great as previous projects would automatically be reported as a copy using bots to remove (not report) it to prevent moderators from taking too much time if they reported. They could also program a second server to take over the job if the first one crashes. Once all the existing copies have been found, it checks new copies going forward.[/quote]\
actually, no it wouldn't be easy to code, while i may not be an expert, i can grasp the complexity of coding it. and we don't want the servers to crash.... ever.....[/quote]\
Yeah, it would be easy to code. First, it checks project 1, 2, 3, etc. until it finds a shared project. It stores that number to continue the count. Then it finds any exact copies. Once taken down, it retrieves the stored number (let's say 10) and then go 11, 12, 12, etc. until it find another shared (not private) project. Continues doing. The project IDs go up by one each time a new project is uploaded or created, so a number must be stored on the server indicating the max projects when it looks for coding. It could also gather the data (sb3 file contents) of all shared projects (which only takes a few seconds for millions of then because of the way computers work), sort them, find the exact copies after it's been sorted in alphabetical order, then go back to the original project (because it records the way the projects connect to the files), and takes down based on sharing date. Medium, but not too difficult.\
\
There is only a limited number of projects that Scratch will ever have. The servers won't be guaranteed to crash unless it's infinite. It's not an infinite loop.

Well, most people share projects without thinking at the bar (which is probably why it got removed), but it may take X years to find inappropriate usernames if they never post one thing. People would probably be more considerate with their usernames because they may see the bar while signing up (because of what portion of the website they're usually in when trying to) sign(ing) up (problems can be anything from slow internet connection to blacklisted IP addresses) which is the front page) and try to avoid alerts and reports. body:
Let's assume that first, someone took the entire lyrics of a copyrighted song; next, used Google Translate to make it French; then, used Microsoft Translate to make the French version Croatian; after that, change it to official grade 2 braille; finally, post it in a comment. And then you notice because you're a real genius/expert in translation websites and can decode it back to the original copyrighted song. You create a report, and next, the moderators alert you and not them. Then you decide to use Contact Us. However, the ST can take days to respond, and by then, you may have lots of daily messages piling up your inbox and they ask you for the link to the comment that you can't find because of all these messages.\
\
So I decided to make this suggestion. Let's assume the suggestion has already been implemented. First, you tell the Scratch Team for the comment to convert it from official grade 2 braille; next, use Microsoft Translate to convert it from Croatian to French; then, use Google Translate to turn it back to English, with the link to the copyrighted song and its license; finally, wait for the comment to be taken down. Although grade 2 braille can only be properly translated by a human and they may take days to find the right person, in the end, it will be gone.

name: What is the ST's exact process for \changing\" usernames?"
body:
[quote=Flowermanvista][quote=kChiaEC19]I need, like, ALL the details: the source code (except for confidential info like server passwords), the order in which it gets changed first, how the exact order works, etc.[/quote]\
I'm not sure what you were expecting, because in all actuality, it's an exceedingly simple process:\
\
The ST creates a new account with the desired username. Then they transfer over all of the user's projects (including comments, studios, description, view count, favorite count, and love count, and all remixes), transfer all of their followers to the new account, and anything else they've ever made or done on Scratch to the new account. They then delete the old account.[/quote]\
But in what specific order? Because they must transfer the user ID, studio and project IDs, comment ID and time, description (both sections), user activity, etc. then delete the old account and make it an available username. All the user settings as well (country, profile picture, email address, comments off for X projects, followers, following, etc.

\
Perhaps there isn't even a defined order, maybe they just issue a \copy account\" command that copies it over in whatever order.

name: How do I make a workaround for the Join ()() block? The Wiki's script doesn't help.
body:
[b]In short words:[/b]\
I need a workaround for this block that can store about infinite (or at least 8,400,000 and more than 200,000) characters in order to store backups properly:\
[scratchblocks]\
(join [] [world])\
[/scratchblocks]\
[b]In long words:[/b]\
So I found this workaround on the Scratch Wiki, and I was told that it would work when I can't use the join block because it can only output the first 10,240 characters of the string.\
[scratchblocks]\
delete all of [final v] :: list\
set [count v] to [0]\
repeat (length of (insert1))\
  change [count v] by (1)\
  add (letter (count) of (insert1)) to [final v]\
end\
set [count v] to [0]\
repeat (length of (insert2))\
  change [count v] by (1)\
  add (letter (count) of (insert2)) to [final v]\
end\
set [result v] to (final)\
[/scratchblocks]\
This works in most cases, however, if you look about lists, they can only hold up to 200,000 items in Scratch 3.0.\

OK. But it may (the extra lists) take up the 50MB limit. Hopefully it doesn't. I'm putting it this way with the hyphen because it needs to know when to add it to the list, as usernames have varying length. Otherwise, if it assumed all usernames were a certain number of characters long, the backups may not restore properly.\
Adding the string to a collection can store 200,000 * 200,000 = 40,000,000,000, way more than the backup's maximum possible length, so it should work. I'll do it when I get home.\
My script will be very close to (there may be slight variations and my script may be messed up):\
[scratchblocks]\
define join (insert1) (insert2)\
set [count v] to [0]\
repeat (length of (insert1))\
change [count v] by (1)\
if <(length of [final v]) = [200000]> then\
add (final :: list) to [finals v]\
delete all of [final v] :: list\
add (letter (count) of (insert1)) to [final v]\
else\
add (letter (count) of (insert1)) to [final v]\
end\
end\
set [count v] to [0]\
repeat (length of (insert2))\
change [count v] by (1)\
if <(length of [final v]) = [200000]> then\
add (final) to [finals v]\
delete all of [final v] :: list\
add (letter (count) of (insert2)) to [final v]\
else\
add (letter (count) of (insert2)) to [final v]\
end\
end\
set [result v] to (final)\
[/scratchblocks]\

[scratchblocks]\
if <(length of [final v]) = [200000]> then\
add (final) to [finals v]\

name: Workaround to Rejected Suggestion: Project Ratings
body:
The rejected suggestion, as explained in [url=https://scratch.mit.edu/discuss/topic/343602/]The Complete List of Rejected Suggestions[/url]:\
[quote=Za-Chary]\
[b]4.2 [url=https://scratch.mit.edu/discuss/topic/196776/?page=2#post-1958521]Dislike button[/url] or [url=https://scratch.mit.edu/discuss/topic/271875/?page=1#post-2749716]a project rating system[/url][/b]\
This idea has a major drawback.  Generally, a user's first project is something rather simple, such as a test project, a remix, or a project made using a tutorial.  Because this project is simple, other users may give the project low ratings since it is not advanced.  With low enough ratings, the creator might be discouraged enough to stop using Scratch, even though the creator is just trying to learn.  \
\
Moreover, constructive feedback is encouraged on Scratch.  A dislike button may show the creator how many people disliked their project, but it tells nothing about what the creator could do better.  If you do not like a project, you could choose not to love it, or you could leave a [i]respectful and constructive[/i] comment telling the user how to improve.\
[/quote]\
The link to the project is:\
https://scratch.mit.edu/projects/352642184/\
[b]Please do not report this project just because the Scratch Team rejected the suggestion.[/b] This is just a workaround, and reporting the project would be unconstructive and disrespectful to the Scratch Team. If enough reports are received for this project, other respectful people may be disappointed to see that the project shows up a 404 error.\
Here are some other reasons not to report this project:\

[*] Only I can see if a specific user rated by typing their username into the popup box when the project starts.\
[*] [b]The server operating the stored ratings for each user in the project is the only one that can see who rated for what.[/b] This prevents online fights, and follows the Community Guidelines because no one else, not even me (the server is operated by haydenledean instead) can see the ratings without looking inside the cloud data logs.\
[*] Not only are people other than haydenledean (-ReadyBoy-) unable see the ratings, they are also unable to see the number of ratings, the number of any one specific rating, or the percentage of each rating versus the total number of ratings.\
[*] The server also checks if the lists are full when posting a rating due to Scratch 3.0's limit on list sizes, and responds back to the user by setting the \response\" cloud variable to the encrypted version of their username and the number 6 right after it.

[*] [b]Share/unshare alert[/b]: Sharing the alert adds an entry to the user activity and appears on the user's followers' What's happening feed. name: (Critical) Topic views
body:
When looking through the forums, you will notice that every topic has a specific view count. However, anyone can spam the view counts by refreshing the page and waiting for it to load, even if they're logged in to the same Scratch account each time or it has been less than one second. In conclusion, every visit counts as a view, regardless of whether or not you visited that topic before. So, someone can organize a private or public group to get people to visit a topic with zero replies many times to millions or billions of views.\
\
I noticed this when I cleared the cache every time.

-Everyone (already selected)\

-Specific people (separated by spaces, commas, or blank lines when typing usernames; any presence of invalid usernames listed will present a warning to the user before adding it to the variable)\

start sound [sound v]::sound\

name: Touching Sprite block returns true for clones
body:
[quote=IsaiahContreras]bump[/quote]\
Please don't bump unless it has been at least 24 hours since the last post and the thread is no longer on the first page in the list of most recently posted/opened threads of that topic. This rule applies everywhere.\
\
Anyway, to answer your question, to be honest with you, this is not your fault. It is not Scratch's fault either. The block intentionally always returns true for clones, because it is useful in certain circumstances. For example, a portal to go to the next level in a platformer can have clones (such as the portal being rendered as clones by turning e.g. squares into circles by creating clones and repeating after rotating multiple times), and the player can check if it's touching ANY portion of the portal (the original or a clone).

name: Transfer Ownership of Studios to the Correct Account
body:
Hold on a second – I just found a disadvantage.\
\
Let's say that your email account gets hacked one day. They look in your inbox and other folders and notice that you signed up for scratch.mit.edu. Even if they don't know your Scratch username, they can still find it out by working logically backwards. They reset your password and enter what email address is supposed to be on your Scratch account, which should most likely still be on your Scratch account (as it usually is). They change the password through the reset password link they received on [b]your[/b] email. After that, they change the email from \their\" (actually your) email to their email (probably one that they created) and sign up or log in to their own Scratch account (also probably one that they created). They change the email on your Scratch account to match their one before you get the email account back; when you find out you were hacked
column4: it's already too late to reset the password. They can then change the ownership and even if you already got your account back (if so
column5: they [b]already[/b] transferred ownership [b]before[/b] the ST changed the email back)
column6: you cannot change it back to yourself because you don't have access to their account. Finally
column7: they delete every studio because they now have the control; even the most popular ones."

body:
Anyone could cause a future argument (even if it takes a few years) if they use a different image hosting service than someone else, like this:\
[scratchblocks]\
when new [forum post v] made :: events hat\
forever\
  if <not <[forum post v] [owner v] uses [CubeUpload v] ? :: sensing>> then\
    repeat until <[forum post v] [owner v] uses [CubeUpload v] ? :: sensing>\
      say [You must use CubeUpload now!!!]\
    end\
  else\
    say [Phew!] for (2) secs\
  end\
end\
[/scratchblocks]\
\
Existing forum posts will stay as-is, and anyone can keep their old accounts. name: The Longest Word in the English Language
body:
I found it on Wiktionary, but had to look up a program to remove (strip out) the zero-width spaces when I noticed them as soon as Google encoded them. It contains 189,819 letters, and is the full chemical name for a form of a protein called Titin. There was a man in a YouTube video that pronounced the word fully, but that took over three hours. Sorry if this is slow for your browser or a duplicate of another topic. The word is:\
\
Whether this is actually a word is still a debate, though. It hasn't gone into any known dictionary yet, but the longest coined term in major dictionaries is pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis. Pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis is a lung disease.\
Sorry if this took up a/some whole page(s). Although 189,819 (the word length) is very close to 200,000, which is the maximum character length for a forum post (the original text, not the BBCode/DjangoBB version), we still need an additional 10,181 characters to fit the entire post, and this remainder shown here should be a lot less than 10,181 characters long.

name: Allow the mouse-pointer to be in multiple places at once (touchscreen)
body:
Hi! I want to make it so that users can select whether the stage can hold one or multiple mouse-pointer positions at the same time. If multiple, the three blocks (mouse x), (mouse y), and <mouse down?> will report a list. The first mouse-pointer will be marked as item 1 in each list, the second as #2, etc — and you can insert these blocks (only these) into the dropdowns. However, if you switch the setting from multiple to one, Scratch should automatically remove it from the list dropdown to prevent the thing from breaking. You also shouldn't be able to just edit the JSON file (project.json), because Scratch should also check and then remove it if needed. This is how it would look like:\
\
[scratchblocks]\
when green flag clicked\
wait until <mouse down?>\
wait (0.3) secs\
if <<(item (1) of <mouse down?> :: list) = [true]> and <<(item (2) of <mouse down?> :: list) = [true]> and <(length of <mouse down?>) = [2]>>> then\
  broadcast [mobile v]\
else\
  broadcast [desktop v]\
end\
[/scratchblocks]\
Actually, there should now be three settings instead of two: one-touch, two-touch, and multi-touch. For everything except for one-touch, the three mouse-pointer blocks should be treated as lists of numbers/booleans converted into strings, instead of reporting a number or boolean. When you have a block like this, though:\
[scratchblocks]\
<touching [mouse-pointer v] ?>\
[/scratchblocks]\
It will also be reported as a list as well. True if the first touch is touching the sprite, otherwise false, on #1 in the list. The same for #2 (except that it's on a different position in a list), #3, the twentieth touch, etc.

name: 3D pen sizes
body:
[quote=ggenije]To calculate distance from camera to some 3D point use Pythagoras theorem:\
[scratchblocks]\
define getDistance (x) (y) (z)\
set [Dist v] to ([sqrt v] of ((((cameraX) - (x)) * ((cameraX) - (x))) + ((((cameraY) - (y)) * ((cameraY) - (y))) + (((cameraZ) - (z)) * ((cameraZ) - (z)))))\
((((cameraX) - (x)) * ((cameraX) - (x))) + ((((cameraY) - (x)) * ((cameraY) - (y))) + (((cameraZ) - (z)) * ((cameraZ) - (z)))))//upward\
[/scratchblocks]\
\
This calculates how far is some point with coordinates x ,y ,z by using  Pythagoras theorem: sqrt((cameraX-x)^2+(cameraY-y)^2+(cameraZ-z)^2)\
\
Then use\
[scratchblocks]\
set pen size to ((yourPenSize)/(Dist))//yourPenSize is adjustable number\
[/scratchblocks]\
This is for one point. If you want to use for line, because you can't change pen size while drawing line, you have 2 options:\
One which is harder and slower and the other one which is easier and faster.\
The first one (harder) is to draw every fragment of line by interpolating value from one part of line to another using two distances but it will be very slow.\
So the only right way is simple to use\
[scratchblocks]\
getDistance(px1)(py1)(pz1) ::custom\
set [penSize1 v] to ((yourPenSize)/(Dist))\
getDistance(px2)(py2)(pz2) ::custom\
set [penSize2 v] to ((yourPenSize)/(Dist))\
set pen size to (((penSize1) + (penSize2)) / (2))\
[/scratchblocks]\
And there is another even easier way is to simple use only distance of the first point.[/quote]\

name: Country detectors
body:
[quote=mtech22][i]-snip-[/i]\
[small]i think it tracks your computer location using ip or something[/small]\
[/quote]\
Determining a country or location from only a known Internet Protocol/IP address is not 100% feasibly foolproof for several reasons (sometimes, the country name can be changed but not the country itself):\
[list=1]\
[*]A computer may be requested to connect to a different object provided by an internet service provider (whether it would be a dial-up modem, an Ethernet cable, a 2.4- or 5.0-GHz-banded Wi-Fi router, a city-wide cellular tower to communicate with mobile devices having an active SIM card in possession, or something else). name: A way to post and turn off commenting simultaneously
body:
Currently, when you make a comment on a profile, project, or studio page within the Scratch website, you send a request to the Scratch servers to post the comment. [i]However, you have to send another request to the Scratch servers[/i] to turn commenting off on that profile, project, or studio page.\
\
[b]But, what if you were able to bind the two requests into one?[/b] This would be useful because the mere fact that commenting is off does not automatically determine the reason why commenting is off, so you would have to make a comment to announce why. [i]This issue is especially prominent on front-paged projects and studios on Scratch because multiple comments are usually made within a short duration period[/i]; currently, you cannot rearrange the order of comments because they're sorted based on the time Scratch added the comments on their posters' behalf.\
\
The best way to implement this is to create a \Post and turn off commenting\" button (not \"Post and Turn (O/o)ff Commenting\" because sentence case strains some people's eyes) right next to the \"Post\" and \"Cancel\" buttons when posting a comment (a \"Post and close topic\" button is useful for the forums). This button should have the same background colour (in Scratch 2.0
column4: button backgrounds are linear gradients) as the Cancel button to avoid confusion with the [i]main[/i]/[i]primary[/i] call-to-action button
column5: but it should have the text colour matching the background colour of the Post button to avoid confusion with the Cancel button using the same text colour ([url=https://uxmovement.com/buttons/why-cancel-buttons-should-never-have-a-color/]source that specifies why buttons without an associated action should not have a colour[/url]).

body:
[quote=Little_Tails]so i have been BLOCKED (a block is where you can make a new account) i tried to appeal a few months ago and you never got back to me saying if i couldnt get it back or if i could[/quote]\
A block and ban are the same thing, but you're not supposed to work around on the block except if only one specific account is blocked (e.g. when someone requested to be blocked just to make a screenshot for the Scratch Wiki). When you are blocked, the Scratch Team blocks every alternate account it can find (but family members can get mistaken for alternate accounts) and new accounts get blocked within 24 hours for working around a block on the main account; sometimes, the Scratch Team even specifies in their appeal responses that blocks and block history are spread across an entire real-life person, not per individual account that breaks the Community Guidelines. Please note that every new conversation sent to appeals@scratch.mit.edu automatically sends an automated response back confirming that Scratch has received it. However, as the OP specified:\
[quote=Flowermanvista][i]-snip-[/i][quote=Back in 2016, cheddargirl]If we're not responding to a ban, it's usually because:\
- the contact e-mail address is fake, or there was a typo in it so it got delivered to the wrong address\
- the banned person's e-mail is not accepting e-mail coming from the @scratch.mit.edu domain\
- the appeal is disrespectful or spammy. Spammy ones can end up being added to an e-mail blacklist, so it's important that the e-mail is not spammy the first time an appeal is sent. \
- the case requires an adult to appeal[/quote]\
[i]-snip-[/i][/quote]\
IP bans should be appealed using the same email address above.\
\

name: What the Email Alert Means
body:
(I promise you this guide isn't random, but it's unique and not unoriginal.) Google did not provide any good answers (even when I quoted it to force searching for the exact word-for-word case-insensitive string), so I had to figure things out myself. If you get the following automated alert below, please hear me out.\
[quote=Messages from the Scratch Team]It appears the email you provided is owned by another person. Please be sure to change the email associated with your account to one you own.[/quote]\
This means that someone logged into your email account and either accidentally or purposely clicked the unsubscribe link, even if it's you. By doing this, the system thinks that you did not authorize a Scratch account to be created with the email address in question, so it sends an alert to all users (including affecting the unread-message-count API of [b]deleted[/b] accounts) reminding you to keep your account settings up to date. This is due to the nature of email providers sometimes recycling email addresses as part of their policies.\
\
[big][b]What do I do if I get this alert? I know that I clicked the unsubscribe link and I can't receive new emails from Scratch when I used to be able to, but I want to.[/b][/big]\
The first thing you should do is log into all your accounts associated with the same email address and close the alert. After you close the alert, it may still show due to your browser cache. However, the next thing you should do is to go to the Contact Us page (especially if you use email aliases), click the \Get Help\" button
column4: and then fill out the Contact Us form
column5: making sure you have the correct email. [b]Do [u]not[/u] delete your email account before this and make sure your email account is fully secure while not locking yourself out.[/b] There is currently a glitch saying that the confirmation or password reset email was sent when Scratch didn't initiate the sending process. The topic selected should be \"Question about notification or blocked account\" → \"Email Confirmation\" (or \"Other\"). Let them know nicely that you accidentally clicked the unsubscribe link (even if you don't get most automated emails from Scratch
column6: you will get automated confirmation responses to new inquiries). The Scratch Team will then remove your email address from their so-called \"Do-Not-Send\" list to allow you to receive new automated emails from Scratch
column7: from resending confirmation emails to password reset emails. [b]Please note that the response times are sometimes delayed during the COVID-19 pandemic.[/b]

name: After the Scratch Team removes your email from their Do-Not-Send list
user_id: request a password reset with only your email address filled in
body: not your username (deleted accounts will not show in the automated email you receive) and make sure you recognize all of the usernames (including the difference between capital i/I's and lowercase L/l's). Do not click the unsubscribe link (you or someone else who logged in your email account already did that earlier either accidentally or purposely) or you will have to start the process all over again
column4: but contact the Scratch Team again if you don't recognize any usernames (set the category to the same as before
column5: but make sure it's \"Email Confirmation\"—not \"Other\"). This way
column6: the Scratch Team can manually notify users who created a Scratch account with your email address to change it (or block those accounts). But reset any passwords that you don't remember from the same password reset email (if applicable). Different accounts for different purposes can have either different emails or the same email
column7: whatever you wish."

name: Unread messages
body:
Even though Scratch 3.0 does not require a page reload for the second page of messages, due to server-side caching the messages stay unread for a bit in case you accidentally clicked on the icon (Scratch 2.0 updates faster), but they eventually go away.\
\
However, I would prefer if there is also a way to mark specific messages as unread (not by clicking on the messages icon without warning), search for messages, and filter out by only unread messages—such as when I want to read newer messages, but still don't have the time to read older messages in a rush due to an IP ban. I wouldn't want the older messages to be marked as read simultaneously just because I read the newer messages, though.

name: Why didn't our account backpacks automatically move from Scratch 2.0 to Scratch 3.0?
body:
[quote=imfh]It’s not as simple as writing a script to update copy the backpack over; the scripts would need to be converted to Scratch 3, the sprites would need to be converted to Scratch 3, everything would need to be modified to work with new backpack system, everything would need to be thoroughly tested to make sure it couldn’t possibly break, then it would have to be run taking up massive server resources. Developing and running the scripts to do all this would take time and server resources which the Scratch Team decided could be better spent elsewhere.\
\
[quote=46009361]Can a Scratch Team member give me more answers? It's been over a minute.[/quote]\
Really? The Scratch Team doesn’t answer questions on demand. They usually only answer if the community doesn’t come up with an answer and they decide to respond. Acting impatient isn’t going to help your chances of the Scratch Team deciding to respond.[/quote]\
I was technically asking the Scratch Team for verification and technical details, as the answers to this question are not so simple. But, considering that they could convert an entire project from 2 to 3, they could've done the same with the backpack. Think about it this way: imagine if someone left Scratch only to find out that their backpack was lost when they came back without knowing it was going to be deleted or warning because they didn't visit Scratch for a while. Clearing backpacks (same with recycling usernames) should become a rejected suggestion. The only thing that might've taken a while to update was the screenshot preview for the backpacked scripts. Costumes/backdrops (previously called backgrounds in Scratch 1.0) and sounds are easier because they're just PNG/SVG files for images and MP3/WAV files for sounds. It is true that the file extension changed from .sprite2 to .sprite3 for compatibility with older compilers' reasons (unlike .pdf, which stays the same when the Adobe Portable Document Format specification changes), as changing the extension assures the older compiler that it doesn't just looked corrupted, but was created differently entirely. The backpack is just a list of named and unnamed costumes, backdrops, scripts, sprites, and sounds (but not entire projects) that are only accessible to the owner of the backpack. They would've been able to convert it had it not been deleted by just converting each file for each person.

column4: I received an email from [b]help@scratch.mit.edu[/b] confirming that a username change had been applied to my account because the old username contained personal information. However
column5: I noticed a caveat with this: my old username was recycled and available for reuse. In this suggestion
column6: I propose for usernames not to be recycled when a username is changed by the Scratch Team because accounts could potentially get hacked on third-party websites (such as [url=https://ocular.jeffalo.net]Ocular[/url]
column7: [url=https://scratch-wiki.info]the Scratch Wiki (international)[/url]
column8: and [url=https://modshare.futuresight.org]Mod Share IV[/url]) that use Scratch accounts to verify account ownership when logging in or resetting your password. Cases like JS_Coder

name: Why didn't our account backpacks automatically move from Scratch 2.0 to Scratch 3.0?
body:
[quote=Austinato][quote=46009361]Although my account didn't exist before Scratch 3.0 was released, the reason why I made this thread was because (over/about) one year ago, I found [url=https://scratch.mit.edu/discuss/topic/322680/]multiple[/url] [url=https://scratch.mit.edu/projects/265112757]sources[/url] that said that the backpacks were going to be removed once the backpack tool and bugs were updated.[/quote]\
Okay? If I understand what you're saying correctly, your question has been answered a few times already. The ST might have just not had the resources to transfer the content. There might be a more technical answer to that, which I can't provide, but that should be a suitable answer for many.[/quote]\
I understand that you aren't able to provide a more technical answer to the question, but let's start with what we know (I'll let anyone take over Austinato's spot if they want to, as this thread is open for practically everyone unbanned to post on). First of all, apart from physically redesigning the interface, moving the project player to the right (I don't like the left as much because people should read the code first in an English-speaking website), and adding new extensions that weren't previously there, the source code also moved from an Adobe Flash applet/object (which you sometimes have to download a plugin/add-on if it isn't already preinstalled, enter the administrator password to install your downloaded file that you opened, and allow your web browser to recognize the plugin and approve it for this session/website) to JavaScript.\
\
Additionally, the [url=https://en.scratch-wiki.info/wiki/Scratch_File_Format]3.0[/url], [url=https://en.scratch-wiki.info/wiki/Scratch_File_Format_(2.0)]2.0[/url], and [url=https://en.scratch-wiki.info/wiki/Scratch_File_Format_(1.4)]1.4[/url] (not even a full-on article with proper details, as there's mostly links to external sites) formats are drastically different from one another. The .sb and .sprite file extensions don't even have a 1 at the end as it was not known in advance at first that Scratch 2.0 would ever be released (or, if so, exactly when it would switch to 2.0 and what the new editor would be like); I might've thought that 1.5 was coming after 1.0–1.4. I'll see if a Scratch Team member has a more technical, in-depth, verifiable (i.e. is possible to prove as fact or invalidate a claim) reason why backpacks weren't just transferred to 3.0. That would've, had the 2.0 backpacks not been gone, just make it much more convenient for anyone expecting their backpacks to be automatically save. Some Scratchers' brains may even be extra super-sensitive to even minor changes (like erasing a hard-worked-on backpack and it's mono-audio and .sprite2 files) that they might seriously contemplate deleting their Scratch accounts and never coming back, or even worse, ending their own lives. After all, losing a backpack you dearly loved just because the database was wiped or corrupted isn't fun for the end user on their client/computer/device, right?

name: Alternate Account Mistakenly Blocked
body:
I created another account called [url=https://scratch.mit.edu/users/KrlsMa/]KrlsMa[/url]. However, when I logged in the next day to delete the account, I found out that the account was blocked. However, the block was a misinterpretation by the Scratch Team:\
\
[url=https://u.cubeupload.com/46009361/AccountKrlsMaBlocked.png][img=https://u.cubeupload.com/46009361/AccountKrlsMaBlocked.png]This was the ban reason. However, I forgot to specify that the account was not intended to impersonate (only to stop impersonation) and that I clarify that I am not (affiliated with) the real KrIsMa.[/img][/url]\
\
How does the Scratch Team not understand that I wasn't attempting to deliberately impersonate on purpose (but to help someone else) and instead just assumed that it was my intention when it really wasn't?

name: Alternate Account Mistakenly Blocked
body:
[quote=VioletCalico]Impersonation is a big issue on scratch, and a lot of times scratchers who didn't impersonate have gotten blocked. For example, accounts that start with griff and have a griffpatch pfp sometimes get banned for impersonation, and I know a scratcher who it seemed like she was pretending to be Hermione, but it was just an RP, and she got banned anway. \
\
The ST does ban people who may seem like they are impersonating even if they are not, so maybe send a message to them and explain what happened so they can unban your alt. account.[/quote]\
Though it is there so that real impersonators can be blocked like a username such as TheRealGriffpatch, it could cause something like LikeGriffpatch to be deleted as the Scratch team may misinterpret the username as \my personality and genetics are griffpatch himself\" instead of \"fan of griffpatch\" — they also even ban joke \"kaj\" accounts."

\

I think Dropbox might be allowed if you use a direct download link (the URL needs to end with [i]?dl=1[/i]) so that you can't access anything other than the file itself, but I'm not sure -- file hosting sites in general could be a problem because it's hard to prevent inappropriate files from being posted.\

body:
[quote=Maximouse][quote=46009361][quote=Maximouse][quote=46009361]What's file.io, by the way?[/quote]\
A file sharing website.[/quote]\
No, like the details?[/quote]\
What kind of details?[/quote]\
Like who it's made by, what exactly does it do, etc. I noticed that file.io appears to be for uploading expiring files, so how do I link permanent files? After all, I sometimes don't want files to expire. I mean, uploading files directly into forum posts is rejected, but certainly people would prefer to have whitelisted links than just disabling files completely:\
[quote=The Official List of Rejected Suggestions][b]9.6 [url=https://scratch.mit.edu/discuss/topic/449439/?page=3#post-4564638]Allow files to be uploaded into forum posts[/url][/b]\
The Scratch Team would have to pay for storage of these files, and they only have a limited amount of resources to do so.  Storage space would be better allocated toward Scratch projects, anyway.  There is also the issue of someone uploading a file that can potentially cause harm to someone's computer.  Searching through these files would require significantly more moderation work, and there are not enough moderators able to do the job at the moment.\
\
[b]10.3 [url=https://scratch.mit.edu/discuss/topic/695/?page=1#post-4569]Remove restricted image hosts or add your own websites[/url][/b]\
By requiring an image host website (such as [url=https://cubeupload.com/]cubeupload[/url]) to be used when posting images on the forums, this decreases the chances of inappropriate images being posted on the forums, as inappropriate images are not allowed on these image host websites.  The Scratch Team does not have the time to whitelist everybody's websites, especially when acceptable websites already exist.\
\
Years ago, the Scratch forums suffered from trolls who continually spammed the forums with highly inappropriate images.  It got so bad that the [[]img] tag had to be temporarily disabled so it could be improved.  [b]Certainly Scratchers would prefer to have to use an image hosting website rather than not being able to post images at all.[/b][/quote]\
Speaking of iCloud below, though:\
[quote=Za-Chary]If iCloud is similar to Dropbox, then I would say iCloud is not allowed, either.[/quote]\
Problem: iCloud requires an Apple ID, in which you have to be 13+ to even create one.
